S1.rationale: Ticket-scoped Codex/Devin model workers implement user software tasks in isolated worktrees, feeding repository/test results into their own decision loops. No independently supported execution bug requires changing the model adapter in this bounded review.

S2.rationale: Planner topological waves and per-ticket worktrees attenuate dependency, repository-write and Git integration interference. Current issue #16 explicitly says conflict detection, sequential merging and non-conflicting continuation are already implemented; do not propose reimplementing these shipped mechanisms.

S3.rationale: Human parent owns current merge-wave admission and approvals, with status and conflict reporting supporting the decision (S3=P). Issues #13 and #16 leave TUI/per-PR select and post-conflict retry/sync follow-ups; they are active native roadmap, but not enough to claim a new assessment-derived current-control gap or select a compatible patch without design scope.

S3*.rationale: Task output and PR quality can be reviewed manually, while first-party code has no independent complementary correctness audit with explicit corrective loop. Generic absence is insufficient to introduce a review agent absent a native failure and maintainer request.

S4.rationale: Ticket intake, status and provider sessions support current project delivery rather than outside/future strategy adoption. A proposed Planner LLM is incomplete at the reviewed ref but was never proven to own organizational S4 or requested for that purpose.

S5.rationale: Project operator chooses base branch, ticket scope, merge policy and approval rights. These are governing deployment parameters but do not create a distinct ultimate-policy agent; no identity-level contradiction has a demonstrated product effect.
